solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Divine player of bridge, for example

parts.note: the four bridge players are named after compass points: North, South, East and West
'say' introduces an example, like 'for example'

explanation.surface: A card player at the bridge table is praised as heavenly, as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' looks like an adjective praising the player, but it is the verb meaning to predict.
explanation.definitionFit: To soothsay is to foretell the future, which is what it means to divine.

clue.text: Absolutely no magic initially in bed

indicators.note: 'no' says the following letter is not wanted, so it comes out of the word

parts.note: 'smack' as an adverb means directly or absolutely, as in smack in the middle

indicators.note: 'initially' points to the opening letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the opening letter of magic, to be removed

explanation.surface: Someone insists there is definitely no magic going on in the bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: SMACK loses its M to leave SACK. 'Hit the sack' is slang for going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sack is informal slang for a bed, as in the phrase hit the sack meaning to go to sleep.

clue.text: Unfinished cabin below old plant

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its ending, so the final letter goes
in a down entry, a piece placed below another comes after it

parts.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old
a shack is a rough cabin; it loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A half-built cabin sits beneath an ancient factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' suggests a factory next to the cabin, but it is the botanical sense: oshac is the Persian plant that yields gum ammoniac.
explanation.definitionFit: Oshac is the name of a Middle Eastern herb, the source of ammoniacum gum, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Trifles of T Moorey all wrong? Drop a line!

definitions.note: plural noun in the clue; the answer is a mass noun for trifling behaviour

indicators.note: letters that are all wrong are out of their proper order and must be rearranged
to drop something is to let it fall away, so those letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written
the setter's name, taken as written
taken as written, before the letters to drop are removed
A as written plus L, the abbreviation for line; these come out of all

explanation.surface: The setter, Tim Moorey, mocks his own clues as trifles and tells himself to drop a line.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL minus A and one L leaves L, which joins OF and T MOOREY to be rearranged. The setter's own name in the fodder is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomfoolery is silly nonsense or trifling, so trifles in the sense of foolish trivialities fit it.

clue.text: Went about work supporting special constable?

indicators.note: in a down entry, the pieces that support another stand below it, so they follow it

parts.note: S is a standard abbreviation for special
'went' as a euphemism for urinated
C stands for circa, Latin for about
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A special constable carried on with their duties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special constable' reads as one phrase, a British volunteer police officer; here 'special' is just S and the question-marked 'constable' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A speed cop is a police officer who catches speeding motorists; a constable is a police officer, hence the question mark for an example.

clue.text: Look north for Aberdonian club

parts.note: an air is a look or manner
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Someone searches the north of Scotland for a club in Aberdeen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' suggests a society, but it is a golf club; airn is the Scots form of iron.
explanation.definitionFit: Airn is Scots for iron, and an iron is a type of golf club, so an Aberdeen speaker's club.

clue.text: Insubstantial indeed, borders on triviality

parts.note: 'yes indeed' — both affirm

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its edges, so only its outermost letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of triviality

explanation.surface: Something flimsy, indeed close to trivial.
explanation.walkthrough: Yesty is a variant of yeasty, frothy like yeast.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesty means frothy and so lacking substance, like the foam on fermenting yeast.

clue.text: Horse, that is to say Silver

parts.note: SC is short for scilicet, Latin for namely or that is to say
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Introduces a horse named Silver, like the Lone Ranger's mount.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lone Ranger's horse is Silver, but 'horse' here is drug slang for heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: Both horse and scag are slang names for heroin.

clue.text: Child training bares bottom on them

definitions.text: Child training bares bottom on them

parts.note: CH is a standard abbreviation for child

indicators.note: training shapes something into a new form, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: the bottom of a word is its end, so its last letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of them, added to the rearranged letters

explanation.surface: A toddler being potty trained sits bare-bottomed on them.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes chamber pots, on which a child in potty training bares its bottom. This is one of four clues in the puzzle that all have the same answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers is short for chamber pots, the potties a small child sits on during toilet training.

clue.text: Prince seen with aged knight, mostly calm

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: AE is short for aetatis, Latin for aged, as on gravestones
N is the chess notation for a knight
easy means calm and relaxed; it loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A prince appears beside an elderly, fairly calm knight.
explanation.walkthrough: Aeneas is the Trojan hero of Virgil's Aeneid.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeneas was a Trojan prince, son of Anchises and Venus, who escaped Troy's fall.

clue.text: Most rank Diana the star in romance years ago

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it

parts.note: a gest is an old word for a tale of adventure or romance
Diana Ross is the singing star

explanation.surface: A singer stars in a terrible old love story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Years ago' marks gest as archaic. Diana Ross goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank can mean gross or flagrant, so the most rank is the grossest.

clue.text: Leaning forward as before, look stern pulling faces

indicators.note: a word's face is its front, so pulling it off removes the first letter of each

parts.note: a cast is a look, as in a cast of the eye; it loses its first letter
the poop is a ship's stern; it loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone bends forward as before, giving stern looks and pulling faces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As before' marks the definition as an old word; 'look stern' reads as an instruction but is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Astoop is an old adverb meaning stooping or bent forward, a posture of leaning forward.

clue.text: Missing father, college student in Surrey town

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: a fresher is a first-year student at college
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest

explanation.surface: A student whose father has gone missing turns up in a Surrey town.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county south-west of London; a fresher is a British first-year undergraduate.
explanation.definitionFit: Esher is a commuter town in the county of Surrey, in southern England.

clue.text: Doctor in search for treatment? Room for diet perhaps

definitions.note: singular in the clue; the answer is used as a plural for a set of rooms

indicators.note: one piece being in the other means it is placed inside
treatment works something over, so the letters are processed into new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine

explanation.surface: A doctor looks for a cure and suggests a room in which to diet.
explanation.walkthrough: A diet is also a legislative assembly, which meets in a chamber; the surface wants it to mean a weight-loss regime.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers is a room or suite, and a parliamentary diet sits in a chamber, as an example.

clue.text: Describing what can be wasted, engineer stabilised pressure for a short time

indicators.note: to engineer is to build or contrive, so the letters are reconstructed
putting one thing for another means it replaces it

parts.note: taken as written
P is the symbol for pressure
T is the shortened form of time, which P replaces

explanation.surface: An engineer temporarily stabilised the pressure in a system.
explanation.walkthrough: In STABILISED the T is replaced by P before the letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissipable means capable of being dissipated, that is squandered or scattered away.

clue.text: Commonly made from a table

definitions.meaning: first meaning: frequently, an old word for often
second meaning, read as three words: composed of a multiplication-table product

explanation.walkthrough: Split OF TEN TIMES, the answer describes something made from the ten times table, as learnt in school.
explanation.definitionFit: Oftentimes is an old-fashioned adverb meaning frequently, and its split reading names a multiplication table.

clue.text: Poet's still evasive, about to retreat first

indicators.note: first places that piece at the front of the answer
retreating goes backwards, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: ca is short for circa, about; reversed and placed first
coy means reluctant to give details, evasive

explanation.surface: A poet remains evasive, about to retreat from an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb but is the verb to calm; 'Poet's' marks accoy as Spenser's word.
explanation.definitionFit: Accoy is a Spenserian verb meaning to quieten or soothe, so a poet's word for still.

clue.text: Australian cricket club away from home about to prepare for a battle?

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation for Australian
CC is the abbreviation for cricket club
out means not at home
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An Australian cricket team on tour is about to gear up for a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an Ashes series between England and Australia; the question mark flags battle as one example of what one might equip for.
explanation.definitionFit: To accoutre is to equip or dress someone, especially with military gear before fighting.

clue.text: Note it's missing out "BAME" — case for revisions?

definitions.text: Note it's missing out "BAME" — case for revisions?

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so those letters are taken off

parts.note: a chit is a short note
taken as written, the letters removed from the note

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or not right, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: a case surrounds its contents, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of revisions

explanation.surface: A note points out that the acronym BAME is not yet listed and is a candidate for the next revision.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue observes that Chambers, the dictionary used for barred puzzles, did not yet include the term BAME (Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic), a case for its next edition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chambers Dictionary is regularly revised, so a missing term is a case for its revisers.

clue.text: Salt type one consumed?

parts.note: a form is a type or kind
I is the Roman numeral for one
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: Asks whether some kind of salt was eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark plays on salt being something consumed.
explanation.definitionFit: A formiate, or formate, is a salt of formic acid, a chemical compound.

clue.text: Fish caught for Sabbath in Manhattan area

indicators.note: one thing for another means it takes the other's place

parts.note: SoHo is a district of Manhattan
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
S is an abbreviation for Sabbath; C takes its place

explanation.surface: A fish is caught for a Sabbath meal in a part of Manhattan.
explanation.walkthrough: The first S of SOHO becomes C.
explanation.definitionFit: The coho is a Pacific salmon species, a type of fish.

clue.text: Director not quite 20 gets Will's "enough said"

indicators.note: not quite all of it means the last letter is left off

parts.note: a score is twenty; it loses its last letter
sese is a Shakespearean exclamation found in Chambers, glossed as enough said; Will is Shakespeare

explanation.surface: A director under twenty is told by Will that enough has been said.
explanation.walkthrough: '20' looks like a cross-reference to another clue but is just the number, twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Scorsese is an American film director, of Taxi Driver and Goodfellas.

clue.text: China firm on American left repeatedly

indicators.note: repeatedly says the idea is given twice, in two different forms

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm
A is a standard abbreviation for American
L is the abbreviation for left
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A pottery company is described as resting on an American who repeatedly departed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country but is porcelain; Coalport is a Shropshire porcelain maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Coalport is a well-known English make of porcelain tableware, so it is a type of china.

clue.text: Very large rodent loses tail containing hard, grey element

indicators.note: losing its tail means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
a mouse is a rodent; it loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A huge rat-like rodent loses its tail while holding a hard grey element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Containing' looks like a container signal, but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmous describes a compound containing osmium, a very hard, bluish-grey metallic element.

clue.text: Independent is carrying leader on Rupert Murdoch

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it inside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of Rupert
I is the abbreviation for independent

explanation.surface: The Independent newspaper runs a leader about the press baron Rupert Murdoch.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants Rupert Murdoch the media owner; the novelist Iris Murdoch is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris Murdoch was an Anglo-Irish novelist and philosopher, so a Murdoch by surname.

clue.text: Liberal in club is a twin

indicators.note: one piece in another means it is placed inside

parts.note: a mace is a heavy club
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A Liberal member of a club turns out to be a twin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twin' is the crystallographic sense, not a sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: A macle is a twinned crystal, two crystals grown together, which mineralogists call a twin.

clue.text: Delivery firm not half late, on reflection tip out

parts.note: UPS is the parcel delivery company

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the wrong way round, so the letters are read backwards
not half means one half of the word is removed

parts.note: taken as written; its first half is removed

explanation.surface: A courier running late decides on reflection to leave a tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' looks like a gratuity; tip out means spill, which is to upset.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset a container is to knock it over, tipping out its contents.

clue.text: Spot around outskirts of Rimini is a top spot

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to spot something is to eye it

indicators.note: outskirts are the edges, so the outermost letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of Rimini

explanation.surface: A place on the edge of Rimini is praised as a top location.
explanation.walkthrough: Rimini is an Italian seaside resort.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is an eagle's nest built high on a cliff, literally a lofty spot.

clue.text: A Baltic rum drunk in retirement

indicators.note: drunk means staggering and disordered, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A retired person drinks rum from the Baltic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In retirement' sounds like old age, but it means withdrawn from public view.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbratical means keeping in the shade, secluded, which is living in retirement from public life.

clue.text: Some kind of square dance

parts.note: a T-square is a draughtsman's ruler
a hey is an old country dance

explanation.surface: Describes a square dance of some kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square dance' reads as one phrase; 'Some' is the definition, the pronoun for unspecified people.
explanation.definitionFit: They, as a pronoun, refers to some people in general, as in they say it will rain.

clue.text: Scottish expert reflected miles away

indicators.note: away means gone, so those letters are removed

parts.note: to muse is to reflect or ponder
M is the abbreviation for miles

explanation.surface: A Scottish specialist thinks about being miles from home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflected' looks like a reversal signal but just means thought.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots usage, used means practised or experienced, so an expert.

clue.text: Mrs Beach composed suite for recorders?

indicators.note: to compose is to put together, so these letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The American composer Amy Beach, Mrs H. H. A. Beach, wrote a suite for recorders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suite' and 'recorders' suggest music; a Recorder is a part-time judge in England, and chambers are the rooms where judges and barristers work.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers are a suite of rooms used by barristers and judges, including Recorders, who sit part-time.

clue.text: Run alongside Russian river in the country

indicators.note: alongside means placed next to, so one piece follows the other

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
the Ural is a river flowing through Russia and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: Someone jogs beside a Russian river out in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural describes things located in the countryside rather than in towns.

clue.text: Film story covering literary hero short of money

indicators.note: covering something means wrapping around it

parts.note: a tale is a story

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so that letter is removed

parts.note: Kim is the boy hero of Kipling's novel
M is an abbreviation for money

explanation.surface: A film's plot features a literary hero who is broke.
explanation.walkthrough: Kim is the orphan boy hero of Rudyard Kipling's novel of that name, a standard crossword hero.
explanation.definitionFit: A talkie is an early film with a soundtrack, so a talking picture.

clue.text: Brand (only two letters of solution required!)

parts.note: the opening pair of letters of solution, S and O, said as letter names

explanation.surface: A puzzle note says only two letters of the answer are needed.
explanation.walkthrough: Saying the letter names S and O gives the sound of the brand name; 'solution' also nods to the answer itself and to the petrol.
explanation.definitionFit: Esso is a well-known petrol brand name, owned by ExxonMobil.

clue.text: Pierced skin of tiny Dee eel caught

indicators.note: caught as in tangled up, so the letters are mixed together
a skin is the outside layer, so only the outermost letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of tiny
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A small eel caught in the River Dee has its skin pierced.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a river in Scotland, and another in Wales and England.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeleted means having eyelets, small holes, so it is pierced with holes.
